Chief_Complaint.content: Right knee pain with clicking after increasing running mileage
Chief_Complaint.source_text: R knee pain w/ clicking after increasing running mileage

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Right knee pain with clicking began approximately 2 weeks ago
Patient is marathon training, started about 1 month ago
Patient runs up to 7–8 miles
Patient goes to the gym a few times per week
Pain is located in the middle of the right knee, sometimes slightly to the right side
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Location: middle of R knee, sometimes slightly to R side

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Pain starts about 20 minutes into a run, around 2.5–3 miles
Patient experiences clicking with knee flexion and extension during abdominal exercises
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: clicking w/ knee flexion/extension during ab exercises

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Pain has been worsening and caused the patient to stop the last run
Patient had mild swelling after the first run which improved with ice
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Swelling: mild swelling after first run; improved w/ ice

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Currently the right knee is not swollen and not painful at rest
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: currently not swollen and not painful at rest

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports the knee is "not bad" in terms of instability and mainly hurts
Patient denies knee locking
Patient denies issues with stairs
Patient has no issues with walking
Patient is able to fully extend and fully flex the right knee
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: ROM: able to fully extend and fully flex

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient had one episode of tingling in the right toes after a run which resolved
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: 1 episode tingling in R toes after run; resolved

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies persistent numbness or tingling in the legs
Patient denies color or temperature change in the legs
Patient denies calf pain
Patient reports occasional sock indentation after standing a long time, suggesting dependent swelling
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Dependent swelling: occasional sock indentation after standing long time

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of prior severe urinary tract infection requiring ER visit with concern for kidney stone
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Prior severe UTI (ER visit; kidney stone concern)

Medications.content: Patient takes ibuprofen up to 400 mg
Patient takes Aleve as stated by patient

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is training for a marathon
Patient plays ice hockey and had a fall with a large bruise a few months ago
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Ice hockey; fall w/ large bruise a few months ago

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient sometimes smokes a joint of cannabis

Assessment.content: Right knee pain with clicking after increased running mileage for 2 weeks, with prior transient swelling, no locking, no functional limitation with walking or stairs, and brief post-run right toe tingling that resolved
Assessment.source_text: 1. R knee pain w/ clicking after increased running mileage x2 wks; prior transient swelling; no locking, no functional limitation w/ walking/stairs; brief post-run R toe tingling (resolved).

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue ice therapy frequently for right knee pain and clicking
Reduce and ease up running and avoid running through pain, especially if needing to stop
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Reduce/ease up running; avoid running through pain (esp if needing to stop)

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient may take ibuprofen as an NSAID
Prescribe a stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly instead of ibuprofen, to be taken with food and not combined with ibuprofen
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • NSAID: OK to take ibuprofen; prescribe stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly instead of ibuprofen (take w/ food; do not combine w/ ibuprofen)

Plan_of_Care.content: Refer patient to physiotherapy for assessment and examination of the right knee
Consider imaging depending on physiotherapy assessment to rule out cartilage issue
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Consider imaging depending on physio assessment (r/o cartilage issue)

Plan_of_Care.content: If physiotherapy wait is too long, patient has the option to be seen in clinic
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • If physio wait too long: option to be seen in clinic

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient advised to seek urgent review if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever or feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and is unable to bend or straighten
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • Urgent review if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or knee locks (unable to bend/straighten)
